entities.name: Pediatric NAFLD
observations: Pediatric non-alcoholic fatty liver disease; biopsy cohorts include steatosis, NASH, and fibrosis phenotypes.

entities.name: Nocturnal hypoxia
observations: Nocturnal obstructive sleep apnea/intermittent hypoxemia is associated with pediatric NAFLD severity and hypoxia-linked liver injury markers.

entities.name: Oxidative stress in pediatric NAFLD
observations: In biopsy-proven adolescents, urinary F2-isoprostanes tracked apnea/hypoxia severity, time with SaO2 below 90%, and lower oxygen nadir; hepatic 4-hydroxynonenal correlated with hypoxia severity and steatosis. OSA/hypoxia was associated with stage-3 fibrosis in 36% versus 0% without OSA/hypoxia (PMID 27501738; n=36 NAFLD).

entities.name: Pediatric OSA liver association
observations: A meta-analysis of 9 cross-sectional studies involving 1,133 children/adolescents found OSA associated with higher ALT, AST, and NAFLD fibrosis stage; ALT/AST associations persisted in age-, sex-, and BMI-matched analyses, but causality was not established (PMID 32881371).

entities.name: CPAP oxidative-stress signal
observations: In 9 children/adolescents with biopsy-proven NAFLD and OSA/hypoxia, about 89 days of CPAP reduced ALT and urinary F2-isoprostanes despite increasing BMI; the uncontrolled before-after design did not demonstrate histologic reversal (PMID 29752170).

entities.name: Hypoxia fibrogenic signaling
observations: In adolescents with biopsy-confirmed NAFLD, OSA/hypoxia was associated with hepatic Sonic hedgehog/Gli2, alpha-SMA, K7, and HIF-1alpha-related signaling that correlated with liver enzymes, NAFLD activity, and desaturation measures (PMID 31334441).

entities.name: PMID:27501738
observations: Biopsy-based pediatric study of nocturnal hypoxia, oxidative stress, and NAFLD progression.

entities.name: PMID:32881371
observations: Meta-analysis of pediatric OSA and NAFLD-related liver outcomes.
